description: Investigate the evolution of the validate_email_domain() function in src/validators.py using Git history. The function has known bugs with international domain handling. Your task: (1) Open src/validators.py and locate the validate_email_domain() function around line 45. (2) Use Git Blame (right-click → 'Git: View Line History' or enable inline blame annotations) to identify which commit modified the problematic lines that contain .strip().upper(). (3) Use VSCode's Timeline view or file history to examine all commits that modified this function. (4) Identify the specific commit that introduced the .strip().upper() logic that breaks international domains. (5) Use 'Compare with Previous' or diff view to understand what changed. (6) Create a file named FINDINGS.md in the project root (/home/ga/workspace/email_validator/) documenting your investigation. The FINDINGS.md file MUST include: (a) The full or partial commit hash of the problematic commit, (b) The author/developer who made the change, (c) A description of what was changed (specifically mentioning .strip().upper() or the modification), (d) An explanation of why this change causes problems (e.g., breaks international domains, case sensitivity issues). Use markdown formatting with clear sections. The commit you're looking for modified the email domain validation logic and was made sometime after the initial implementation. Save the FINDINGS.md file in /home/ga/workspace/email_validator/ when complete.
